Videos

Source: vignettes/articles/videos.Rmd
videos.Rmd

Two series of short videos about amorem. Every number on screen is computed by running the package; the narration is in English.

Night Sky Atlas

One real dataset per card, seen as a night sky: actors are stars, each event is a streak of light between two of them, and time runs along the horizon. Each card ends on one finding computed with amorem. The cards stand alone and can be watched in any order.

No. 1

Over Washington

Every leader-to-leader visit of the United States, 1945–2019. A country whose leader has just visited Washington is about twice as likely to be the president's next stop (2.08 times the rate, 95% interval 1.60 to 2.69).

Try it in R: amorem::us_leader_visits

Time, Rate, History

Eleven short lectures that build relational event models from the ground up: events, rates, history as a covariate, the partial likelihood, case-control sampling, smooth effects, goodness of fit and global covariates. They are meant to be watched in order. They also play on the Luche channel on YouTube.

Episode 1

The data are events, not a network

A relational event model starts from a log: who acted towards whom, and when.

Episode 2

Every pair has a clock

Give every ordered pair its own exponential clock.

Episode 3

Coefficients multiply rates

Each pair's rate is a baseline times exp(beta times x).

Episode 4

History becomes a covariate

Endogenous statistics turn a log's own past into covariates: reciprocity, transitivity, recency and their variants.

Episode 5

Which dyad fired?

Given that an event happened, which pair was it? The partial likelihood asks only that question.

Episode 6

Compare with a few who did not

The partial likelihood sums over every pair at risk.

Episode 7

How many controls?

How many non-events should be sampled per event? On a fixed history, more controls narrow the spread of the estimate without moving its centre: from one control to ten, the spread falls about three times.

Episode 8

Ghosts read the past but never write it

A sampled non-event did not happen, so it must read the history to get its covariates but must never write into it.

Episode 9

With one control, a regression on differences

With one control per event, the conditional logit becomes a logistic regression without intercept on case-minus-control differences.

Episode 10

Is the model wrong?

Rank the candidate models by AIC on one shared case-control sample, then check the winner.

Episode 11

Why the weekday cancels

A covariate shared by every pair at the same moment, such as the weekday or El Nino, takes the same value for an event and its controls, so it cancels like the baseline.
